summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old woman was admitted after a mechanical fall resulting in a right intertrochanteric hip fracture, which was repaired with cephalomedullary nailing. Postoperatively, she developed hypotension and troponin elevation consistent with a Type 2 NSTEMI, managed with aspirin, heparin, and beta-blocker up-titration. A pharmacologic stress test revealed new reversible ischemia in the RCA and LAD territories, but cardiology recommended medical management over intervention. She experienced postoperative ileus with colonic distention, managed conservatively with bowel regimen adjustment. Her chronic ITP led to transient postoperative thrombocytopenia without significant bleeding, and she received a single-unit blood transfusion for anemia in the setting of CAD. An asymptomatic UTI was treated with a short course of ciprofloxacin. Renal function, initially impaired, normalized with diuresis. She was discharged to rehabilitation with optimized cardiac and pain medications, DVT prophylaxis with heparin, and close follow-up plans.
problems: Closed fracture of intertrochanteric section of neck of femur
